teaching.hint: A replacement can affect which of the original bad adjacencies?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Each originally violating adjacent pair needs an edited endpoint; the 26-letter alphabet always permits one edited letter to satisfy both neighboring pairs.
solution_outline.approach: Scan the original adjacent pairs from left to right. On a violating pair, charge one edit to its right position and skip the next pair that this edit can also cover.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Charged bad edges are pairwise vertex-disjoint, while chosen edited positions cover every original bad edge.
solution_outline.correctness: Disjoint charged edges force at least one edit each. A replacement avoids at most six forbidden letters from its two neighbors, so every selected edit can fix its incident pairs; the matching construction attains the lower bound.
solution_outline.pitfall: Counting every bad pair separately overcounts runs such as three equal letters, where one edit repairs two pairs.

common_wrong_turns: Editing once for every bad pair
Assuming replacement letters can be unavailable
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; clarified alphabet adjacency and that only the edit count is returned.
